00:00 Lena: okay everyone, thanks for joining, this is Lena from Redwood, i'm the account lead. quick round of intros?
00:12 Dr. Maya: hey i'm Maya, cto at Peregrine Health, we run clinical note summarization and some triage flows.
00:20 Evan: Evan, lead ML eng, i'll own the dataset and bench runs.
00:24 Sophie: Sophie, SRE, i'll own infra questions.
00:28 Samir: Samir from Redwood, i'll do the deep dive on perf and cost.
00:33 Lena: sweet — goal today is to align on success criteria and cost targets for a 6-week POC, specifically unit economics so you can justify an ops budget.
00:42 Tom: timeline sounds good, we have a pilot commitment from product if cost looks right.
01:05 Samir: to start, can you describe your expected traffic profile? qps, burstiness, token sizes?
01:12 Evan: yeah so average we see about 0.7 rps per concurrent user, for POC we expect peaks at 10-15 rps, sustained 3-5 rps. Typical note input 200-300 tokens, generation target ~150-250 tokens, so call avg ~420 tokens. some long notes 900+ tokens but rare.
01:40 Lena: cool, so for sizing we should plan for peak 15 rps with headroom. what's your SLO? p95 latency?
01:48 Dr. Maya: target p95 under 200ms for front-end interactive flows, p99 under 500ms is ideal but we can degrade for heavy items.
01:58 Samir: noted. Quick callout on architecture — caching/prefix KV cache can pull down token work for repeated templates; if you have many repeated templates we can get big wins.
02:10 Evan: we do reuse templates a lot, but not the whole note. will caching help if only prefix repeats?
02:16 Samir: yes. KV cache saves previously computed key/value states, so for multi-step chat or templates it avoids recomputing. Practically you might see 15-40% token reduction depending on repetition.
02:29 Sophie: any gotchas with KV cache and privacy? we need to ensure cached keys don't persist beyond session TTL.
02:36 Samir: absolutely — cache TTL configurable, and on private/dedicated deployments cache can be encrypted and purged on demand.
02:44 Evan: ok, on to cost — what's the ballpark per-token on hosted vs dedicated?
02:50 Samir: rough numbers for discussion: hosted baseline per-token compute cost for the model we propose is about $0.0006 per token (this includes GPU inference and infra overhead), so per-call at 420 tokens ~ $0.25. With batching and KV cache you can reduce effective per-token by 20-60% depending on concurrency and cache hit rate. On dedicated reserved capacity with optimized int8 kernels and aggressive batching you can get effective $0.00015-$0.00025 per token at scale.
03:18 Dr. Maya: so for a pilot with budget ~ $5k / month, how many calls is that?
03:25 Samir: simple math — at $0.25 per call that's 20k calls. With batching/caching to $0.12 per call that's ~41k calls. On dedicated at $0.06 per call you're at ~83k calls. These are illustrative — we'll run exact modeling for your QPS and token distribution.
03:48 Lena: important note — latency vs cost tradeoff: larger batch sizes increase throughput and lower cost but add queueing latency. for interactive SLOs like p95 < 200ms we need small batch windows (10-30ms) and that limits batching savings. for background summarization you can use larger batch windows.
04:10 Tom: could we hybrid? host interactive on hosted with strict SLO and route batch jobs to dedicated?
04:16 Samir: yep that's a common pattern: route low-latency paths to smaller, low-batch nodes and bulk jobs to high-batch dedicated pools. Redwood routing can do policy-based fallback.
04:28 Evan: for benchmarks, what configs should we run?
04:32 Samir: plan: 1) baseline single-request latency p50/p95/p99 hosted; 2) batching sweep (batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16) to show cost vs latency; 3) KV cache on/off; 4) cold start vs warm; 5) sustained 15 rps soak for 30 min to check tail latencies. we'll produce per-token cost and per-call cost tables.
05:00 Sophie: we need to be sure about network and VPC options — we can't send PHI to a multi-tenant hosted service unless certified.
05:08 Lena: understood — do you need Private (VPC) for pilot or can you use hosted with SOC2 controls and a BAA?
05:16 Dr. Maya: for pilot we'd prefer hosted with a BAA if possible, otherwise a private deployment. security folks will decide but we need SOC2 and audit logs.
05:26 Samir: Redwood has SOC2 and can sign BAA; for Private we can provision a VPC-controlled control plane or on-prem later. we'll include compliance docs in the pack.
05:36 Evan: about dedicated pricing — is there an upfront commit?
05:40 Lena: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits. for pilots we often do a small reserved month-to-month pool or short-term credits to run benchmarks. we'll model both scenarios.
05:50 Tom: any specifics on quantization impact to latency/accuracy? we care about hallucination behavior on clinical text.
05:58 Samir: quantization to int8 typically gives 2-3x speedups and lowers memory, sometimes with minor quality delta. we'll run quality checks against your eval set. if we see regressions we can try mixed-precision or higher-bit quant. we'll tie quality regressions back to eval thresholds as part of success criteria.
06:18 Evan: can you share a sample cost model spreadsheet?
06:21 Lena: yes i'll send a spreadsheet showing per-token math, batching scenarios, and a dedicated vs hosted comparison with example budgets.
06:27 Samir: for the benchmark metrics we'll return a table with columns: model variant, batch size, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per sec, cost per 1k tokens, effective cost per call, cache hit rate scenarios.
06:42 Sophie: one more ops ask — do you support RBAC and SSO for the console?
06:47 Diego: yes console supports SAML SSO and role-based access; audit logs available for Private.
06:52 Dr. Maya: ok, last piece — success criteria: we'll track 1) latency p95 < 200ms for interactive flows, 2) QA metric (ROUGE/F1 or human eval) within 2% of our baseline, 3) POC cost below $5k/month or clear path to < $2k/month at scale.
07:14 Lena: good, we'll formalize that in the POC doc and include acceptance tests.
07:20 Tom: timeline — can you run the hosted baseline by next week?
07:23 Samir: yes we'll start as soon as we get the anonymized dataset. Evan?
07:27 Evan: i'll upload 5k anonymized notes and a traffic profile by Friday (2026-07-16).
07:31 Lena: perfect. to recap quick next steps: lena sends pricing + docs, samir runs hosted benchmarks, evan uploads data, sophie confirms compliance contact. then we reconvene week of 2026-07-27 to review.
07:48 Dr. Maya: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
07:51 Lena: thanks all. bye.
